1
REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences
on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Twenty-sixth Report of the Department-
related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and Forests on
the Demands for Grants (2012-2013) of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, which was presented to
both the Houses of Parliament on 18
th May, 2012. There were twenty-two recommendations in the
Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee were
received from the Department on 27
th July, 2012.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee
on the action taken by the Ministry of Earth Sciences are set out in the succeeding paragraphs:-
Recommendation (Para 5.3)
The Committee feels that without any financial and administrative powers, the Earth
Commission will hardly be effective in performing its role and functions and the very purpose of
setting up of Earth Commission would be defeated. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
immediate steps be taken to provide necessary financial and administrative powers to the Earth
Commission so that it may carry out its assigned role effectively.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing the gratitude to the Committee for supporting the proposal on administrative and
financial support to Earth Commission, the Ministry would like to apprise the Committee that a
draft Cabinet Note of the proposal on administrative and financial powers to the Earth Commission
has already been circulated to all the concerned Ministries/agencies. Currently, their comments on
the same being obtained from the concerned Ministries.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the comments of the concerned Ministries/agencies would have
been received by now and a decision taken. The Committee reiterates its view that administrative
and financial powers be granted without any further delay to the Earth Commission.
Recommendation (Para 6.3)
The Committee notes with satisfaction that Result Framework Document (RFD), has been
adopted by the Ministry to review and monitor physical and financial progress/achievements of
major activities with respect to agreed targets fixed for each programme, in addition to its internal
monitoring mechanisms. The Committee is of the opinion that an effective monitoring mechanism
is imperative for ensuring that the various projects are completed as per the projected schedule and
timely action taken to overcome problems that may arise in the implementation of the projects. The
Committee hopes that with potent monitoring mechanisms, the Ministry would be able to complete
its projects in time.
Action Taken by Government
As pointed out by the Committee, the Ministry has adopted an adequate monitoring
mechanism (3-tier) to monitor the effective performance of various schemes towards timely

2
accomplishing the targets of the projects, including RFDs for all the centres of the Ministry. At
Ministry level, the Earth System Science Organisation (ESSO) Council set up by the Ministry meets
twice in a year to review in detail the performance of various programmes which are generally held
in April and September in the beginning of the financial year and middle of the year. Besides, the
performances of major projects are being monitored by Project Management and Advisory Council.
The progress of autonomous bodies of the Ministry is also monitored periodically by Finance
Committee, Governing Bodies and Research Advisory Committee, besides being monitored by the
Planning Commission on annual basis.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that effective monitoring would lead to
timely completion of projects.
Recommendation (Para 7.3)
In this connection the Committee would like to invite the attention of the Ministry to its
204
th Report (page 3, para 5.1) on the Demands for Grants (2010-11), wherein it has been stated
that as per information furnished by the Ministry, the total initial Budgetary allocation of Rs.7004.00
crores for the Eleventh five year Plan was revised to Rs.6637.00 crores at the mid term appraisal
stage. In comparison to this, the Committee has observed that the projected amount has been
increased by almost three times during Twelfth Plan with outlay proposed by the Ministry at
Rs.18,824.00 crores. The Committee also notes that for focused attention and securing effective
implementation, Ministry has reoriented its 76 projects into 15 major programmes for Twelfth Plan.
The Committee hopes that with increased allocations and more focused attention, the Ministry
would be able to achieve capacity for reliable weather forecasts at par with the highest international
standards and would be able to develop technologies needed for effective exploitation of marine
resources for the socio-economic development of our people during the Twelfth Plan period.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry would like to assure that every effort would be made to achieve the targets
set for Twelfth Five Year Plan, in a more focused way. These included providing reliable weather
forecast at par with international standards, as the numerical weather forecast models, being
employed to develop these weather products by the Ministry, are similar to global models used by
the advanced countries. Besides, more local data collected from the autonomous platforms/sensors
would be assimilated into these models, which will enhance weather forecasting capability. Similarly
the various technology being developed by the Ministry to harness marine resources are the state-
of-the-art technology used elsewhere.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and is of the view that increased demand for budget
allocation, should be matched by proper utilization of funds on the part of the Ministry.
Recommendation (Para 7.4)
The Committee also notes that two projects viz. Multi-channel Seismic System on board
Sagar Kanya and National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT) extension centre in West Bengal,
could not be completed during the Eleventh Plan period. The Committee would like Ministry to
make all possible efforts to complete these programmes as soon as possible and well before the
expiry of the first year of the Twelfth Plan.

3
Action Taken by Government
It may kindly be noted that the above mentioned two projects have been dropped in
consultation with the Planning Commission. However, the objectives envisaged under the projects
could be pursued through existing ongoing programmes of the Ministry without jeopardizing the
goal of these projects.
Comments
The Committee expresses its concern that two of its projects pursued during the
Eleventh Five Year Plan have been dropped without assigning any reason. The Committee
hopes that as assured by the Ministry, the objectives envisaged under these projects would
be pursued through existing programmes of the Ministry.
Recommendation (Para 8.2)
The Committee observes that the Ministry has received a plan outlay of Rs.1281.00 crores,
which is Rs.369.00 crores less than the amount of Rs.1650.00 crores, projected by the Ministry.
The Committee, however, notes with surprise and concern that Twelfth Five Year Plan of the
Ministry is yet to be finalized and the Ministry is not certain about some of the new initiatives that
it had proposed during the Plan period. The Committee recommends that all possible efforts may
be made to finalise the Twelfth Five Year Plan of the Ministry at the earliest so that future roadmap
of the Ministry’s action Plan becomes certain and it can vigorously pursue the Plan targets and
achieve them.
Action Taken by Government
As recommended, finalization of Twelfth Five Year Plan proposals of the Ministry has been
completed and waiting for the final approval of the Planning Commission. Meanwhile the Ministry
has been actively engaged to seek the necessary approvals/clearances of the Government on various
Schemes proposed for implementation during Twelfth Plan.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Ministry after obtaining the approval of the Planning
Commission will make all out efforts to achieve the targets set for the Twelfth Plan.
Recommendation (Para 9.3)
The Committee notes that various ongoing projects/activities and proposed new initiatives
have been integrated into 15 broad major restructured programmes to carry out the research
activities in a more focused way. The Committee hopes that the new initiatives does not lead to
less focused monitoring or neglect of some of the programmes vis-a-vis the position existing so
far when these programmes were assigned individual budgetary allocations. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Ministry should carry out a review, after a suitable interval, to see
if the new system has helped/achieve/improved meeting of physical and financial targets and apprise
the Committee of the finding of such a review. The Committee would, however, like Ministry to
ensure that despite amalgamation of a large number of projects/schemes in a programme, individua1
focus and attention continues to be provided to each schemes and project of the Ministry.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry would like to assure that all the ongoing and new schemes proposed for

4
implementation during Twelfth Plan would be implemented under the 15 Major umbrella schemes
without losing the focus of the individual activities. The necessary review mechanism has been in
place to monitor these activities separately.
Comments
The Committee is not satisfied with the reply furnished by the Ministry. The
Committee’s recommendation was meant for proper scrutiny and critical appraisal of new
monitoring mechanism.  The Committee therefore, reiterates that the Ministry should
immediately carry out the review of its activities/programmes to ascertain as to whether the
new system has worked as per expectation.
Recommendation (Para 10.4)
The Committee has always stressed upon the need for greater application of technologies
for socio-economic development of common masses. The Committee, therefore, commends the
initiative of the NIOT in using technology i.e. ‘Low Temperature Thermal Desalination (LTTD)’ to
solve the drinking water problem in two islands of Lakshadweep, by setting up two LTTD plants.
The Committee is also happy to know that NIOT, also proposed to set up six more plants in other
islands of Lakshadweep, through public-private partnership mode. The Committee is of the opinion
that such technologies needs to be popularized and such plants should also established in Andaman
& Nicobar Islands as well and other coastal regions of the country, which face a scarcity of fresh
drinking water. It also feels that the adoption of the public-private partnership model would make
the establishment of such plants more cost effective, and enable the Ministry to commission a
larger number of plants in the coastal regions of the country in a short time.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing gratitude to the Committee for appreciation, it is informed that the Ministry has
been making several efforts for popularizing the LTTD technology in selected coastal location and
island territories. NIOT has already taken steps to commission six more plants based on LTTD
technology in Lakhshadweep islands (Amini, Chetlet, Kadamath, Kalpeni, Kiltan and Andrott).
Efforts are underway to set up a LTTD plant with a capacity of generating two million litres of
freshwater per day (2 MLD) at Tuticorin.
Comments
The Committee hopes that proposed commissioning of six more LTTD plants in
Lakshdweep Islands and Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu), would be carried out as per schedule. The
Committee reiterates that technologies for the benefit of common man such as LTTD needs
to be encouraged and established in other coastal regions of the country like Andaman and
Nicobar Islands, which face a scarcity of fresh drinking water. It reiterates that the Ministry
may explore the public-private partnership model for setting up more such LTTD plants
which would make it more cost effective.
Recommendation (Para 10.8)
The Committee commends the efforts of the Ministry in augmenting the scientific and
technological capabilities of the INCOIS, in respect of predicting cyclones and tsunami, since
accurate and advance warnings about these natural hazards give sufficient time to disaster
management agencies to gear themselves better to minimize the loss of property and lives. The
Committee is also happy to note that the Indian Tsunami Warning System has been entrusted the

5
responsibility to, function as Regional Tsunami Service Provider by UNESCO and have started its
operation for the Indian Ocean Rim countries. The Committee commends the Ministry for making
accurate predictions on recent earthquake that hit certain parts of India and saving the country
from unnecessary anxiety and fear. The Committee appreciates the fact that the technological
capabilities of the INCOIS have been recognized internationally and hopes that, in future the Centre
would forge collaborations with similar scientific organizations of the advanced countries, to
provide ocean information and advisory services to society, industry, Government agencies and
scientific community through sustained ocean observations, information management, and focused
research.
Action Taken by Government
Thanking the Committee for the appreciation on work of augmentation of ocean information
services, it is mentioned that INCOIS would make every effort to forge cooperation with similar
similar scientific organizations of the advance countries, when ever required to provide best
possible ocean advisory services.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 10.14)
The Committee notes the importance of the useful research being done by the IITM and
hopes that the Institute would successfully provide research backup needed for raising the
accuracy levels of our weather and climate forecasts to the highest international standards well
before the end of Twelfth Five Year Plan and the Committee recommends adequate budgetary
support during the period be provided to the Institute to achieve this task.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry highly appreciates the recommendations of the Committee for the adequate
budgetary support to be provided to achieve the task of providing the research backup needed for
raising the accuracy levels of our weather and climate forecasts to the highest international
standards well before the end of Twelfth Five Year Plan. Some of the major actions taken towards
achieving the targets are (i) establishment of capacity to make dynamical prediction of seasonal
mean monsoon using coupled model (ii) An empirical system to predict the active and break spells
3-4 weeks in advance has also been developed. The High Performance Computer (RPC) of 70
Teraflop acquired by the HTM during the Eleventh Five Year Plan has provided great opportunity
for R&D that has gone in to the improvement in modeling work for weather and climate forecasts.
In order to work out a Modeling Framework and put it in use to predict seasonal mean climate
in India the Ministry has launched a Monsoon Mission with a view to design a weather prediction
model for improving the Indian monsoon weather and climate forecasts, ultimately to develop an
Indian Model (based on changes made to the CFS model) which will have the capability to better
simulate and predict the monsoon rainfall. High priority has been accorded to the development of
climate models for more reliable projection of climate change in the 21 st century – with a special
focus on the behaviour (frequency and intensity) of extreme events (heat waves, cold spells, severe
thunder storms, tropical cyclones, storm surges, severe storms, droughts, etc.) in the near future.
The development of a coupled modeling strategy as well as to generate a large ensemble of future
climate change scenarios using a suite of global and high resolution regional climate models
involves a large number crunching capability.

6
Comments
The Committee appreciates the efforts and the progress made by the Ministry for
improving accuracy of weather and climate predictions. It also notes that the Ministry has
launched ‘Monsoon Mission’ a weather prediction model for better simulation and prediction
of the monsoon rainfall. The Committee hopes that efforts would also be made to pass on
the crucial cyclonic predictions/early warnings to the common man so as to avert any loss
of life and property.
Recommendation (Para 10.11)
The Committee is aware of National Centre for Antarctic and Ocean Research’s (NCAOR)
good performance in conducting scientific expeditions to Polar Regions. The Committee hopes
results of scientific studies being done in .Polar Regions would find useful application in glaciers
of Himalayas, forecasts and control relating to monsoons and in other areas and a better
understanding of climate change would emerge from these studies.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing gratitude to the Committee for the appreciation on scientific performance in
Polar Regions, it may be noted that the results of the scientific studies conducted in the Polar
Regions and the expertise gained out of it is planned to be extended to the Himalayan Glaciers
during the Twelfth Five Year Plan. NCAOR has initiated a long term programme on ‘Cryosphere
studies in Himalayas’ which is intended to conduct Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) traverse,
studies on Snow and Ice Chemistry and Glacier dynan1ics of selected glaciers to begin with. This
would help us in better understanding of the impact of the climate change on the Himalayan Glaciers.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 11.20)
The Committee, is of the opinion that research in the field of cloud physics should be
accorded high priority as it would not only help in right selection of clouds for seeding but would
help master its other aspects as well including development of cost effective techniques for
successful cloud seeding, which may go a long way in helping the country solve the problems of
drought and water scarcity in certain parts of the country. Such research may also provide greater
insights in understanding the dynamics of global warming. The Committee, therefore, strongly
recommends that Ministry should make all our efforts to strengthen the special laboratory which
has been set up at Mahabaleshwar to study all kinds of clouds from precipitation point of view
so that cost effective techniques for artificial precipitation could be  developed and for that, if
needed, adequate funds should be made available.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry expresses gratitude for the recommendations of the Committee for adequate
budgetary support towards strengthening the special laboratory at Mahabaleshwar for addressing
the issues relating to clouds to understand complex interactions between aerosols, clouds and
circulation. It may be noted that the construction of the laboratory will commence after the
monsoon season is over in the month of October, 2012 and expected to be completed by June,
2013. The High Altitude Cloud Physics Laboratory will house the state of art instruments for the
observations.

7
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and at the same time hopes that the construction of
the laboratory would have commenced and would be completed as per schedule.
Recommendation (Para 12.3)
The Committee is happy to note that allocations made for R&D activities of IMD and for
the programmes ‘Research, Training, Education and Outreach’ taken together are sufficient and
hopes that a strong research backup would be available for the Ministry to complete its various
programmes and achieve its objectives during the year 2011-12.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing thanks to the Committee for its appreciation for the activities being carried out
under the programme on “Research, Training, Education and Outreach”, it is informed that during
2011-12, the Ministry had taken several initiatives to support academic programmes, establishment
of national lab facilities, capacity building through opening of training schools, national and
international collaboration etc. These have helped in achieving the objectives of the various
programmes of the Ministry.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Paras 13.5 and 13.6)
The Committee fully understands that though it may not humanly possible to completely
control the forces of nature like earthquake, yet through technological interventions the massive
destruction and financial losses it causes can certainly be minimized. The Committee, therefore,
feels that, intensive efforts towards scientific research are needed to fully understand the various
aspects of earthquakes, it is, therefore, imperative to establish a separate institutional mechanism
to effectively deal with earthquake related issues in the country, so as to minimize the damage in
future due to earthquakes.
The Committee also notes that presently, various aspects of seismology related research are
being carried out in a fragmented way by several research, academic, State and Central
Government institutions in the county. In view of the extreme killer and destructive potential of
earthquake as a natural phenomenon. the Committee fully endorses the proposal of the Ministry to
set up a separate research institute of the nature of ‘National Centre of Seismology’ which is
exclusively devoted to study of the mechanic of earthquakes, geo-tectonic movements and -all
other aspects of earthquake so as to avoid/minimize the losses of life and property, a field which
is yet to be mastered by the human mind.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry is actively considering setting up a National Centre for Seismology (NCS) with
a view to conduct focused research in the area of seismology. It may be mentioned that issues
relating to preparation, circulation of Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) document, finalization
of site/land/construction of building and modalities of setting up of NCS is under consideration.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the procedural aspects relating to setting up of the

8
“National Centre for Seismology’ would be expedited and the Centre established at the
earliest, for carrying out concerted research in the field of seismology, so as to minimize
loss of life and property caused due to earthquakes.
Recommendation (Paras 14.7 and 14.8)
The Committee is of the opinion that the agricultural economy of the country is immensely
affected by the vagaries of nature. However, this effect can on]y be minimized with scientific
inputs, through the installation of state-of-the-art weather observation system throughout the
country and utilizing them for providing accurate and advance information to the farmers pertaining
to the weather and climatic conditions. In this connection the Committee appreciates the Ministry
for initiating the ‘Agro-meteorological services’ to provide advance information to the farmers
pertaining to wind, temperature, rainfall, humidity and soil moisture and help them to plan the
cultivation and harvesting of various crops and in issuing district-level bulletins to 560 districts
across the country. The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Government intends to increase
the coverage of farmers under the agro-meteorological services from the current level of 10% to
around 40%.
The Committee recommends that the Ministry should develop Atmospheric Observations
Systems Network and Atmospheric Processes & Modeling and Services throughout the country in
a time bound manner so as to improve weather and climate forecasting services. The Committee
further recommends that agro-meteorological advisory services should be extended to cover all
districts of the country. The Committee further recommends that crop and location specific
information to farmers be disseminated in a more friendly manner and its reach extended to cover
all farmers in a time-bound manner, so that even small and marginal farmers could full benefit of
these services.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing the gratitude to the Committee, the Ministry would like to inform that at present
127 Agro-Automatic Weather stations have been installed to issue more accurate advisories to the
farmers. In addition to that, Automatic Weather Station recently installed at various locations are
also used for the same. The observations from these automatic weather stations are extensively
used in the preparation of crop and location specific advisories for the farmers. Implementations
of various programmes, popularization of the Agromet Services are being made to outreach these
services to the maximum number of farmers in the country. Efforts will be made to increase user
network of this service.
Under the modernization programme of IMD, efforts are being made to improve the
forecasting system by installation of more weather observations and introduction of different high
resolution indigenous and other models available in different parts of the world. For improving the
outreach of the advisories, the same are sent through SMS and IVRS mode to the farmers in
different States in PPP mode. The advisories will also be disseminated on line through the Farmers’
Club under the network of National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD). Apart
from these, advisories are also disseminated using already existing channels like internet, print
media, Door Darshan Kendras, AIR and other cable TV networks to communicate the Agromet
Advisories to the huge number of farmer in a user friendly manner. IMD shall provide any support
if required for full implementation of the recommendations.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

9
Recommendation (Para 15.3)
The Committee appreciates the good initiative of the Ministry in providing the fishermen
advance advisories, which have led to reduction of search time and increase in the catch per unit
effort, resulting in an increased net profit from 1.5 to 2.5 times and fuel savings upto 30%. The
Committee also note the proposal to increase the user base of these advisories from the existing
65% to 90% of the fishermen across the country, by the end of the Plan period. The Committee
desires the Ministry to make concerted efforts to achieve this target.
Action Taken by Government
Expressing the gratitude to the Committee for the appreciation on fisherman advisory
services, the Ministry will make every effort to augment user base of the Potential Fishery zone
advisories and to reach out fisherman community.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Ministry would be able to achieve
its objective of increasing the user base from the existing 65% to 90% of the fishermen
who are beneficiaries of these advisories, by the end of the Plan period.
Recommendation (Para 16.2)
The Committee feels that there is an urgent need for making concerted efforts to improve
the accuracy of out weather and climate services. In a country like India, where a large section
of population is dependent on agriculture for its living, correct and reliable weather prediction well
in advance, will prove a boon for the farmers. The Committee, therefore, feels that instead of
putting a distant plan of achieving the United States level of accuracy, in climate and weather
forecasting in the next five years, the Ministry should make all out efforts to improve our weather
and climate prediction services and bring them at par with the highest international standards of
accuracy within the next three years.
Action Taken by Government
Towards this, a five day district level Medium Range Weather Forecast is being issued since
June, 2008. During recent years, there is considerable improvement in quality of the forecast
issued. Continuous efforts are being made for improvement of the quality of these forecasts to
bring them at par with the highest international standards or accuracy. During Twelfth Five Year
Plan, it is also proposed to develop and issue block level Medium Range Weather Forecast for
facilitating the preparation of block level Agromet advisories as per the need of the marginal and
small farmers.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the proposal for the development and issue of block level
Medium Range Weather Forecast, to facilitate the preparation of block level Agromet
advisory services would be pursued and completed as per schedule, keeping in mind the
benefits that would accrue to the marginal and small farmers.
Recommendation (Para 17.5)
The Committee acknowledges the significance of the Indian polar missions as the climatic
conditions in these regions have a direct bearing on the monsoons, which is the lifeline of the

10
agriculture in our country. The Committee commends the setting of the Indian polar stations which
would increase the base of data collection regarding polar processes. The Committee hopes that
Bharati station would be commissioned as per schedule and start its operations during the year
2012-13, which will give significant boost to India’s polar research programme. The Committee
recommends that the continuing long term approved scientific projects which are the proposed
activity under the “Polar Science and Cryosphere” should be pursued diligently and in a well-
planned and strategic manner and the data collected from its scientific expeditions must be analyzed
and a serious endeavor made to use the results to predict the Indian monsoons more accurately.
Action Taken by Government
Thanking the Committee for appreciating the setting up of new Indian Station’ Bharati’ in
Antarctica, it is informed that the station has since been operationalised and first team has already
commenced wintering in the station. The collection of scientific data on weather parameter and
Geomagnetic Observation has already commenced.
Comments
The Committee congratulates the Ministry for the operationalisation of the new
Indian Station ‘Bharati’ and hopes that India’s polar research programme would reach new
heights and would help in the accurate prediction of the Indian monsoons.
Recommendation (Para 18.4)
The Committee, notes with concern that there was a shortfall in utilization of allocated funds
by the Ministry, to the tune of Rs.1.24 crores in the year 2009-10 and Rs.2.54 crores in the year
2010-11; which is evident from the difference in B.E. and Actual allocations for the said years. The
shortfall in utilization, is even more apparent for the year 2012, where the B.E. allocation stood
reduced from Rs.18.00 crores to Rs.2.00 crores only, i.e. a drastic reduction of about 90 per cent
of allocated budget. The Committee takes a serious view of the under utilization of funds in last few
years by the Ministry, which shows that the Ministry is not seriously pursuing this important
programme viz.. Polymetallic Nodules Programme. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends
that the Ministry must actively pursue this programme and the programme must be carried forward
with full vigour, for exploitation of the mineral resources in our vast Exclusive Economic Zone to
enhance availability of sufficient mineral resources required for our industrial growth.
Action Taken by Government
Recognizing the past financial performance of the programme, the Ministry has taken up
advance action to identify for chartering of a research vessel towards conducting topographic
survey of EEZ. Another partner has been identified to accelerate the work. The drastic under
utilizations of funds particularly during the year 2011-12 could be due to non-availability of required
chartered research vessel.
Comments
The Committee feels that the procedural requirements such as requirement of
chartered research vessel, ought to be sorted out without any further delay and the funds
allocated for the purpose must be utilized meticulously.
Recommendation (Para 19.4)
The Committee observes that as regards the detection and quantification of  gas-hydrates,

11
major portions of  the deep-water regions have remained unexplored and available data is inadequate
for the assessment of  gas-hydrates. The Committee therefore recommends that evaluation and
quantification of  gas-hydrates must be intensified in the EEZ region of  the country to fully explore
this resource especially in view of  its potential as clean fuel resource. The Committee is of  the
opinion that to meet the ever increasing demand of  energy in the country, it is imperative to explore
alternate sources of  energy as soon as possible and therefore such programmes should be actively
pursued and adequately funded.
Action Taken by Government
Ministry is already working on developing technologies for exploration. The Autonomous
Coring system has been developed and trials are continuing. Similarly remotely operated submersible
has been developed for exploration of  gas hydrates. Presently there is no technology available for
extraction of  gas hydrates from deep waters.
Comments
The Committee notes the efforts of  the Ministry and reiterates that the exploration
of gas hydrates should be expedited to meet the ever increasing demand for energy.

and Industrial Research on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Twenty Seventh
Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology,
Environment and Forests on the Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department of Scientific and
Industrial Research which was presented to the Rajya Sabha on 18
th May, 2012.

of the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received
from the Department on 29
th August, 2012.

1
REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Scientific
and Industrial Research on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Twenty
Seventh Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and
Technology, Environment and Forests on the Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department of
Scientific and Industrial Research, presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 18
th May, 2012.
There were fifteen recommendations in the Two Hundred and Twenty Seventh Report of the
Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the
Department on 29
th August, 2012.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee
on the Action Taken by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research are set out in the
subsequent paragraphs:–
Recommendation (Para 3.3)
Mechanism to Monitor and Review the Ongoing Schemes
The Committee is happy to note that the Department has put in operation a monitoring
mechanism which has helped it to make almost full utilization of allocated funds. The
Committee appreciates the fact that the Department achieved very high composite value scores
of 95.84% and 95.97% consecutively in two years with Excellent grade which reflects the
degree to which the DSIR has been able to accomplish success in its programmes and
schemes. The Committee, however, hopes that the Department continues and maintains this
performance in future as well.
Action taken by Government
The Department notes the remarks of the Committee with satisfaction.
Department’s score in Results Framework Document (RFD) for the year 2011-12 has been
93.90%.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply given by the Department and hopes that in the years
to come the Department would not only maintain its good performance on Result
Framework Document (RFD) but would further improve it.
Recommendation (Para 4.2)
Performance in the Eleventh Five Year Plan
The Committee finds that the BE total allocation of Rs.13044.00 crore for the Department
for Eleventh Plan was enhanced to Rs.13,198.75 crore at R.E. stage implying an additional
availability of funds to the extent of Rs.154.75 crore and is happy to note that the Department was
able to utilize an amount of Rs.13,177.45 crore thus leaving only Rs.
 21.3 crore unutilized. The
Committee hopes that even in future the Department would continue making all out efforts to
gainfully utilize the allocation made to it.

2
Action Taken by Government
The Department appreciates the observations of the Committee and it would take all the
necessary steps towards gainful utilization of the funds allocated to it during the current year.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department.
Recommendation (Para 4.4)
“The Committee is surprised to note that while the Plan outlay earmarked for the
Department for the Eleventh Five Year Plan was Rs.9000.00 crores, the actual allocation made was
curtailed to Rs.6959.00 crores – a cut of Rs.2041.00 crores, more than the outlay for anyone
financial year during the plan. The Committee observes that against the total outlay of Rs.9000.00
crores for entire plan allocation, the RE. allocation was to the tune of Rs.7150.00 indicating a
shortfall of Rs.8l50.00 crores. It is all the more surprising for the Committee because the
Department has been efficiently utilising the allocations made to it throughout the entire Plan period.
The Department was in fact able to utilise over 99 per cent of the allocated funds.”
Action Taken by Government
The Department notes the Committee’s comments.
Comments
The Department has not furnished any reason for reduction of its allocation at
Budgetary Estimate (B.E.) stage. The Committee, however, hopes that the Department would
make optimum utilisation of funds allocated to it.
Recommendation (Para 4.5)
The Committee expresses its anguish over such a huge cut resorted to by the Planning
Commission in plan outlays of the Department charged with the onerous responsibility of using
scientific innovation and interventions for catalyzing the industrial growth making possible
provisions of affordable health care for all and improving the living standards of people at the
bottom of economic pyramid. The Committee is of the opinion that such a step on the part of
Planning Commission is not justified. The Committee, therefore, recommends that such cut
measures should be avoided in future and it must be ensured that the entire outlay for the Twelfth
Five Year Plan is actually made available to the Department.
Action Taken by Government
The Department appreciates the concern of the Committee over cut imposed on plan outlay
of the Department.
Comments
The Committee desires that the Department should take up the issue of huge cut
in Plan outlays with the Planning Commission and impress upon the Commission to
realistically view the requirement of the Department in the Twelfth Five Year Plan and
bring the concern expressed by the Committee to the notice of the Planning
Commission.

3
ACHIEVEMENTS OF CSIR
Recommendation (Para 5.1.2)
While the Committee lauds CSIR for wining a number of prestigious awards at the national
level, the Committee desires that CSIR scientists should strive hard to make their presence felt even
at the international level by winning prestigious international awards as well. The Committee further
desires that with a good number of patents, CSIR should make efforts to help Indian Industry
develop more and more globally competitive products, for that alone will determine usefulness of
patents developed by CSIR scientists.
Action Taken by Government
The Department is thankful to the Committee for its appreciation for winning prestigious
awards. The Department is taking all the necessary steps to help Indian industry in developing
globally competitive products through transfer of technology and process know-how.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply but would like CSIR scientists to win prestigious
international awards and help Indian Industry to develop globally competitive products on
a regular basis. The Committee further observes that steps being taken in this regard
should have been spelt out in its Action Taken Note.
Recommendation (Para 5.10.2)
Technopreneur Promotion Programme
The Committee appreciates achievements of the Department both in high-end technology
and technologies for the societal benefits particularly in affordable healthcare during the Eleventh
Five Year Plan. The Committee, however, feels that a lot more needs to be done if the country
is to emerge as a technology driven economic superpower. The Committee, therefore, desires that
the Department should further intensify and galvanise its efforts during the Twelfth Plan to make
India a truly technology and innovation driven society.
Action Taken by Government
The Department is expanding the scope of the Technopreneur Promotion Programme
(TePP) in the twelfth five year plan to support innovations in the Micro, Small and Medium
Enterprises (MSME) sector and start-up companies, besides individual innovators. Since MSME
sector accounts for 45% of the manufacturing output, 40% of exports, provides employment to
over 60 million people and constitutes more than 95% of the industrial units in the country, seeding
innovations in the MSME sector will help the country in becoming technology and innovation
driven society.
Comments
The Committee is happy to note the expansion of Technopreneur Promotion
Programme and hopes that Department would ensure that the programme achieves its goal
of making India a technology and innovation driven society.

4
Recommendation (Para 7.2)
Budgetary Allocation for the Twelfth Five Year Plan
The Committee finds it quite surprising that even when the Twelfth Five Year Plan has
started, Planning Commission is yet to finalise the Twelfth Plan allocations. The Committee feels
that such a delay could affect not only the Planning and distribution of resources of the Department
but also the physical and financial targets set by the Department. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that Planning Commission should finalise the allocations for the Twelfth Five Year Plan
without any further delay so that the Department is clear on its long term and short term targets
to be achieved during the plan period.
Action Taken by Government
The Department appreciates the concern of the Committee.
Comments
The appropriate course of action for the Department was to bring the
recommendation of the Committee to the notice of the Planning Commission for necessary
action, but it has failed to do so. The Committee expects that now the Department will bring
to the notice of the Planning Commission the concern expressed by the Committee towards
delay in finalisation of Twelfth Plan allocations by the body. The Committee reiterates that
Planning Commission should finalise allocations for the Twelfth Five Year Plan of the
Department without any further delay.
Recommendation (Para 8.4)
OUTLAY PROPOSED AND ALLOCATION APPROVED FOR 2012-13
(i) The Committee is of the opinion that cuts would have an adverse effect on the CSIR vision
and strategies for 2022. Paucity of funds would compel the Department not only to tone
down targets set for the year but even adversely impact realisation of its long term
objectives. The shockingly high cuts indicate that scientific organizations are being given
step motherly treatment in allocation of resources. The Committee is of the opinion that the
axe of such a huge cut should not fall on scientific Departments as it adversely affects
Research and Development which is vital for the development and well being of the nation.
Action Taken by Government
The Department appreciates the concern of the Committee.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Department will take up the matter with the Planning
Commission/Ministry of Finance for restoration of funds at Revised Estimate stage.
Recommendation (Para 8.5)
(ii) The Committee hopes Government would, while allocating funds at RE stage and for
subsequent years, adopt a more rational and judicious approach in allocation of funds and
would ensure that for good schemes, adequate funds are made available. The Committee
feels that support to cluster innovation centres, innovative proposals from MSMEs,

5
upgradation of photovoltaic module from 10 to 80 MW are important initiatives and making
them suffer from financial crunch would not be in the national interest. The Committee is
of the view that considering the conventional sources of energy like coal and petro products
are causing irreparable damage to the environment leading to climate change, it is high time,
that non-conventional sources of energy like Solar energy are encouraged and enhanced.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that Planning Commission must ensure that crucial
programmes like upgradations of photovoltaic module are not starved of funds and adequate
allocations be made to these programmes at the R.E. stage.
Action Taken by Government
Central Electronics Limited (CEL), a Public Sector Enterprise of the Department is
planning the upgradation of solar photovoltaic module production facility from 10 to 80 MW
during the twelfth five year plan, which will help it to make available cost effective solar modules
to the Indian consumers. The Department has requested CEL to submit its precise requirement
of funds for the project during the Financial Year 2012-13 and beyond. Department will request
the Planning Commission/Ministry of Finance at the RE stage to ensure adequate fund allocation
for the project.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that Central Electronics
Limited (CEL) would make available cost effective Solar Photovoltaic Modules to Indian
consumers in a fixed time frame.
Recommendation (Para 8.6)
(iii) The Committee also hopes that DSIR would make optimum use of funds made available to
it and provide to the people of the country best returns for funds invested in it.
Action Taken by Government
Department notes the Committee’s observation for compliance.
Comments
The Committee notes the assurance of the Department.
Recommendation (Para 8.8)
While CSIR allocation accounted for as high as 49.95 per cent and 42.56 per cent
respectively in Third and Fourth Five Year Plan, it had come down to 11.04 per cent in Ninth,
10.18 in Tenth and 11.95 per cent in Elventh Five Year Plan. From Seventh Plan, when all the
existing scientific Departments, were in existence, the share of DSIR has decreased of from 18.29
per cent to 11.95 per cent in Eleventh Plan which indicates diminishing importance of DSIR
vis-a-vis other Scientific Departments. The DSIR, therefore, needs to introspect the reasons for
this state of affairs and must revitalize and gear itself to regain its lost importance. It must prove
its importance for the country by its achievements. The Committee, however, feels that a higher
allocation of plan funds for scientific Departments is absolutely essential for realisation of vision
of making India a knowledge based economy by the end of second decade of twenty first century.
The Committee, therefore, recommends higher overall availability of funds (as% share of plan) for
scientific organisations.

6
Action Taken by Government
The Department, with humble request, would like to add – “Figures are as given in the
Planning Commission website.” The Department notes the recommendation of the Committee.
Comments
The Committee expresses its displeasure over the casual manner in which the Action Taken
Note in the context of the above recommendation of the Committee has been prepared and
furnished to the Committee. Instead of introspecting reasons for diminishing importance of DSIR
in terms of Government funding vis-a-vis other Scientific Departments and taking up the matter
of higher allocation of Plan funds for the Department with the Planning Commission/Ministry of
Finance, the Department has opted to disown the figures. It is immaterial for the Committee
whether the figures are as given by the Planning Commission or the DSIR as both of them form
a part of Government of India and figures were given by the Department in its presentation
document (Page No. 13) on Demand for Grants 2012-13. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its
recommendation and expects the Department to pursue with the Planning Commission/Ministry of
Finance for higher allocation of funds for the Department.
Recommendation (Para 9.1.4)
PROGRAMMES/SCHEMES OF THE DEPARTMENT
A. PROGRAMMES OF DSIR
Technology Promotion Development and Utilisation Programme (TPDU)
The Committee is aware that investment of over Rs.l 0000 crore in R&D had been reported
under this programme and DSIR had reported innovations in various fields like development of Fuel
Cell Bus; E-waste Recycling and Precious Metal Recovery; Indigenous Dialysis Device; Novel Plant
tissue culture medium from bio-waste-Fly Ash; Herbal Medicine for treatment of Asthma; and
A V AZ-Device for Cerebral Palsy through this programme. The programme has now been scrapped
as need for more innovative mechanism was felt for achieving significant results. The Committee
hopes that four new schemes now introduced would be able to produce significant and much better
results than obtained under TPDU and for the purpose, the Committee recommends that
Department should effectively monitor these schemes so that money invested in these schemes is
not only adequately justified but also provides the desired results.
Action taken by Government
The Department shall allocate the funds for the four new plan schemes judiciously and
monitor the progress of activities under the schemes effectively to achieve the planned targets.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that significant results
would be visible from the investment of over Rs. 10,000 Crores in R&D under programme.
Recommendation (Para 9.1.8)
(ii) The Committee feels that in view of budgetary constraints, there is a need for the
Department to devise innovative ways for funding these schemes. Public Private Partnership
(PPP) model, levy of appropriate user charges, funding from other beneficiaries, sharing of

7
profits arising from commercial exploitation of patents funded under scheme, etc. are some
of the known ways in which requisite funds for implementation of scheme can be
generated. The Committee hopes that the Department would be able to devise innovative
ways of funding the scheme and achieve the targets set for 2012-13 under these schemes.
The Committee, however, feels that Government should, to the extent necessary, provide
adequate funds for these schemes at RE stage, so that target set for 2012-13 under these
schemes get realized in toto .
Action Taken by Government
The Department is in the process of obtaining the necessary approvals for the schemes and
shall be able to mobilize the necessary funding for the same.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Department would have by now obtained necessary approval
for its schemes and would be able to mobilise adequate funding for its projects.
Recommendations
B. PROGRAMMES OF CSIR
(I) National Laboratories Scheme
The Committee, in its 208
th Report, had recommended that the network of National
Laboratories should be extended to all the states of the country, with at least one laboratory in each
state so that there is equitable scientific progress in each State. The Committee had also
recommended that though the National Laboratories are doing a lot of ingenious work as regards
Research and Development in various scientific spheres but most of its achievements are not
reaching the common man. In fact, the Committee had felt that the Department of Scientific and
Industrial Research could justify an increase in the budgetary allocation only if substantial benefits
reach the common man and had accordingly recommended that the Department should focus
towards transfer of technology from the National Laboratories to the society.
The Department, however, in its Action Taken Note defended its stand by saying the CSIR
transferred its developed technologies regularly to industries through its constituent laboratories.
Some technology transfers at that time included improved process for centchroman (a non-steroidal
oral contraceptive); treatment of Bio refractory wastewater without sludge and odor emission.
While the Committee appreciates the fact that transfer of some technologies had taken place but
transfer of just few technologies is not going to make the desired impact. The CSIR, with a large
scientific manpower at its command, needs to transfer innovative technologies in a large number
so as to help common man improve his living standard. The CSIR must pay rich dividends to the
common citizen of this country by way of transfer of appropriate technologies for every rupee
invested in its schemes.
Action Taken by Government
During Twelfth Five Year Plan, the Department proposes to establish five new institutes.
CSIR and its constituent laboratories are home to cutting edge scientific capabilities, talent,
know-how and IP. To further enhance the capability and to explore newer models of bringing
processes, products and services to the markets, an independent company named ‘CSIR Tech
Private Limited (CTPL)’ has been incorporated in Pune. CTPL would work closely with CSIR labs

8
to commercialize CSIR technologies and intellectual property through creation of spin-outs and
licensing opportunities based on scientific discoveries emanating from CSIR laboratories.
Comments
The Committee notes the initiative taken by the CSIR to explore and to further
enhance its capabilities by incorporating a company named ‘CSIR Tech Private Limited
(CTPL) and hopes that this new venture would result in effective commercialisation of CSIR
technologies.
Recommendations
II. National S&T Human Resource Development
The Committee observes that allocation made under this head was Rs.307.00 crore at B.E.
stage 2011-12 which got slightly reduced to Rs.305.00 crore in B.E. 2012-13. The Committee finds
that out of the allocated amount of Rs.307.00 crore at B.E. 2011-12, the Department could utilize
only Rs.285.00 crore. This may, perhaps be one of the reasons for lesser allocation has been made
this year under this head. The Committee hopes that Department shall be able to make full and
effective use of funds allocated to it this year.
The Committee notes that the CSIR has introduced 250 CSIR hand holding scholarship for
dyslexic (Attention Deficit Disorder) students to pursue higher education in science. The Committee
feels that this is a very praiseworthy initiative that needs to be further extended and expanded. The
Committee therefore, recommends that this scheme should not cover only dyslexic students but
those suffering from other serious physical disabilities as well.
The Committee feels that institution of greater number of scholarship for higher studies in
science shall to certain extent help in arresting the recent trend of large number of bright students
not opting science subjects for higher studies in view of attractive opportunities that have emerged
in other disciplines and which in turn is leading to shortage of scientific personnel in the country.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that there is a need for further increasing the number of
scholarships as also for making scholarship more attractive. The Committee, further, recommends
that a very transparent, fair and objective criteria be devised for awarding these scholarships so
that meritorious students alone get it.
Action Taken by Government
The initial allocation during the financial year 2011-12 was Rs.307.00 crore (Rs.197.00
crore under Plan and Rs.110.00 crore under Non-Plan) for this head. The Department could have
utilized the allocation of Rs.307.00 crore fully and effectively, however, Ministry of Finance
imposed a cut of Rs.1 00.00 crore on Plan allocation and Rs.58.18 crore on Non-Plan allocation
on the department. Accordingly the Department imposed a cut of Rs.22.00 crore (Rs.7.00 crore
on Plan and Rs.15.00 crore on Non-Plan) for this activity thereby reducing total budgetary
allocation to Rs.285.00 crore which has been fully utilized during financial year 2011-12. Efforts
are being made to utilize the full grant allocated during the financial year 2012-13.
The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. The students suffering from other
serious physical disabilities will also to be covered under this scheme subject to getting requisite
budgetary allocation.
Efforts are being made continuously by the Department to attract more number of bright
students to opt science subjects for higher studies through various fellowship schemes. CSIR has

9
increased the number of Junior Research Fellowships (JRF) by two folds during the Eleventh Five
Year Plan period (2007-12) over the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07) through CSIR-UGC National
Eligibility Test (NET) scheme with regard to qualification and validity of CSIR JRF to widen the
scope of NET and to attract students at early stages of their career. CSIR has also increased the
number of Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Fellowships (SPMF) from the financial year 2012-13 which
is being offered to certain top ranking NET qualified candidates. Besides NET, CSIR has other
fellowship schemes such as JRF-GATE, Senior Research Fellowships, Research Associateships,
Senior Research Associateships and CSIR-Nehru Science Postdoctoral Research Fellowships for
attracting and retaining students in science.
A very transparent, fair and objective criterion is being followed to award the fellowships
through CSIR-UGC NET conducted twice a year with the objective to identify and nurture young
scientific talent to pursue Ph.D. programmes. NET qualified students are being sought by both
academic and R&D institutions across India.
Comments
The Committee is pleased to note that the Department has agreed to the proposal of the
Committee to widen the ambit of its 250 CSIR handholding scholarships to the students suffering
from other serious physical disabilities.
Recommendation
III. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND TECHNOLOGY MANAGEMENT
The Committee is happy to know that CSIR’s rate of licensing/commercialization of
Intellectual Property at about 9% is much better as compared to the global average of 3-4% and
compliments CSIR for it. The Committee, however, feels that there is a need for wider and more
effective dissemination of products/technologies developed by CSIR and patents registered by it so
that common man could be benefited from this knowledge. The Department may consider making
details of all products/technologies developed by it available on its website and organizing seminars
and exhibitions in different parts of the Country to make people aware of them. Advertisements/
handbills and poster campaigns can also be deployed appropriately to create awareness.
Action Taken by Government
The Department appreciates the compliments of the Committee regarding higher rate of
licensing/ commercialization of its IP vis-a-vis  global average. In most of CSIR laboratories,
advertisement and awareness with regard to patent/technology/know-how is usually carried out
through the Institute websites, publications such as annual reports, newsletters, special pamphlets
and brochures. Patent/business development related awareness programmes are sometimes included
in short term courses/Entrepreneur Development Programme undertaken by the lab, both for the
entrepreneurs as well as students. Patents filed and granted are available in the Annual report of
CSIR.
Technology awareness meets are also arranged and users/interested manufacturers are
invited in these meets for interaction with inventors/business development groups. Technology/
know-how developed are also displayed on the Institute website. Advertisement and awareness are
also arranged through Seminars/conferences/workshops, events/exhibitions, internet networking.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department.

10
Recommendation
IV. NEW MILLENNIUM INDIAN TECHNOLOGY LEADERSHIP INITIATIVE (NMITLI)
The Committee finds that this programme was allocated Rs.70 crares at B.E. 2011-12 which
was reduced to Rs.50.00 crares at R.E. 2011-12 but again enhanced to Rs.60.00 crores at B.E. 2012-
13. Noting that programme is to be run on PPP model, the Committee hopes that the Department
would effectively leverage the funds allocated to obtain desired outcome under the scheme.
The Committee has been informed that the reason behind NMITLI Scheme not performing
as expected is that the country is not able to recognize and appreciate the concept of PPP for
Research & Development for R&D. In addition, there is no enabling mechanism to develop
seamless team between industry and publicly funded institutions. It has, further been informed that
the Department proposes to broaden the NMITLI scheme in the Twelfth Plan as per the Cabinet
Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approval.
The Committee is of the view that the Department should take necessary steps to dispel
the apprehensions about PPP mode and make sincere efforts to ensure success of this model.
Action Taken by Government
Fluctuations in NMITLI Budget over the years are due to following:
Funds under NMITLI are utilized timely and effectively. On occasions, Finance Ministry
imposes cut on Department’s budget at RE stage. This cut has to be borne by various programmes
of the Department including NMITLI. For example-Finance Ministry had imposed a cut of Rs.1 00
crore in the budget of CSIR at RE stage for the Financial Year 2010-11. Considering the same and
creating a possibility of funding some of the NMITLI projects in the beginning of the next Financial
year, a cut of Rs.25 crore was employed to NMITLI. It shifted thus taking up of some of newer
projects to Financial Year 2011-12 and utilized the funds within permissible time.
NMITLI is a robust Public Private Partnership (PPP) Scheme in the R&D domain in the
country. It has been able to network about 100 industry partners and about 300 R&D groups from
different institutions. Realizing the success of the model, other government departments are emulating
it. After NMITLI, PPP has become a buzz word in the echelon of Science & Technology. NMITLI
will take every possible step to further strengthen the scheme and ensure success of model.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that as assured, the Department would
further strengthen NMITLI Scheme.
Recommendation
V. CSIR 800
The Committee notes an allocation of Rs.50 crore to CSIR 800 scheme. The Committee,
however, feels that to make real impact on the lives of the poor people, hundreds of such
institutions/initiatives are required. The Committee hopes that the Department would gear itself to
meet this challenge and recommends that Government should extend adequate financial support to
the Department to meet it.
Action Taken by Government
CSIR has geared up itself to meet the challenges expected during the implementation of the
CSIR-800 Scheme. The allocated amount would be utilized in making concerted efforts for bringing
about quality, affordability and prosperity for all, through relevant S&T interventions and
technologies. The allocations would be utilized in establishing CSIR TECHVIL and for initiating new

11
projects in the seven focus domains: Value Added Agriculture, Waste to Wealth, Energy Efficiency,
Low Cost Housing, Affordable Health, Potable Water and Sustainable Energy. The TECHVIL and
associated projects are expected to augment income of individuals and improve quality of the life
during Twelfth plan period. A small part of allocation would be spent in establishing and supporting
new linkages and partnerships with different Line Ministries, Philanthropic Organizations, Financial
Institutions and Channel Partners like Non Government Organizations, V oluntary Organizations, Self
help Groups and Social Entrepreneurs, so as to reach the unreached.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that projects taken in seven focus domains
shall help augment income of people and improve quality of life with visible impact during
Twelfth Plan period.
Recommendation
VI. CSIR Scheme for open Innovation
The Committee, however, is pained to note that programme such as scheme for open
innovation which aims to provide affordable medicines for common man diseases has seen a cut
of Rs.93 crore in allocation. The Committee feels that reduction in allocation to a programme meant
to benefit common man should have been avoided. The Committee, further, recommends, adequate
allocation be made to this programme at R.E. stage so that the programme does not suffer for
want of adequate funds.
Action Taken by Government
The Department notes the recommendation of the Committee.
Comments
The Committee reiterates that sufficient funds be made available to the programme
at R.E. Stage and the Department should take up this matter with the Planning
Commission/Ministry of Finance.
Recommendation
VII. NA TIONAL CIVIL AIRCRAFT DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (NCAD)
The Committee hopes that formal Government approval for the programme would be
available soon and the programme would start in right earnest at the earliest. The Committee is also
of the view that this programme is of great national importance and sufficient funds be made
available to this programme so that our own indigenous 90 seater aircraft becomes a reality in a
short time from now.
Action Taken by Government
In order to identify an enabling (entity) structure for implementation of the National Civil
Aircraft Development (NCAD) programme, CSIR constituted two expert committees. The two
committees are as follows:
(i) Technical Committee to build NCAD programme: The said committee will examine the
feasibility Report and create a document for NCAD programme implementation. It will
also prepare a Cabinet note for obtaining ‘In-principle’ approval from the Government.
(ii) Joint Venture Creation Committee to interact and negotiate with the industry: This
committee will identify and discuss with industry for firming the Joint Venture with
equity participation in design and development and for setting up production facility
and marketing of 90 seater Civil Aircraft under NCAD programme.

12
Further, the NCAD programme will be taken up, in case desired partnerships are built and
due approvals are received.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Department would be able to find a suitable partner
to take the National Civil Aircraft Development (NCAD) programme forward.
Recommendation
VIII. INTERACTION BETWEEN INDUSTRY AND CSIR
The Committee is happy to learn that CSIR has implemented all the recommendations of
Abid Hussain Committee. The Committee notes that share of public funding for R&D at 2-3 per
cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is at par with international norms. However, the share of
private funds for R&D at only 3 per cent of GDP in our country is very low as compared to
international norms of 1.3-1.4 of GDP. In France, Industry performs over 63 per cent (of all R&D)
and funds around 54 per cent projects while this figure is 69 per cent in Japan. In India
contribution of industries is estimated at around 25 per cent of national R&D expenditure which
needs to be enhanced to at least 50 per cent in the Twelfth Plan. The Committee feels that the
Department should give more and more incentive and form more partnerships with the private
sector companies of India in order to infuse more funds in R&D sector. In this regard, the
Committee fully supports the recommendations of the Planning Commission in its ‘approach paper
on Twelfth Five Year Plan-Faster, Sustainable and more Inclusive Growth’ wherein it has suggested
on interaction of Public S&T Institutions with CSIR at large.
Action Taken by Government
The Department is trying to bring industries on board in many plan projects being proposed
to be executed during Twelfth Five Year Plan.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that CSIR would soon
be able to work in partnership with other big industrial players in its endeavour to increase
the share of private funds for Research and Development activities.
Recommendation (Para 10.4)
Audit Objection
The Committee taking serious note of the above observations made by the CAG
recommends that these deficiencies need to be addressed by the Department in right earnest as
such cases bring bad repute to CSIR and this does not put DSIR in right stead. The Committee,
further, recommends that the Department should strengthen its monitoring mechanism so that
misuse of funds could be prevented.
Action Taken by Government
The observations of the Committee have been noted for compliance.
Comments
The Committee would like the Department to ensure such cases do not occur in
future and audit objection is duly settled to the satisfaction of the Comptroller and Auditor
General of India.

13
MINUTES
